title: Learn the Shim Sham - for Lindy Hop and Swing Dance

method.teacher_system: Laura Glaess introduces the Shim Sham as a foundational solo jazz dance. She breaks down the routine piece by piece, demonstrates with front and back perspectives, and guides learners through follow-along practice with music.
method.signature: Demonstrating the choreography simultaneously in front and back perspectives using split-screen editing.

practices.what: Clapping hands to practice the rhythm and identify the 8th count where the moves start.
Dancing through the first move, the Shim Sham, with side-by-side front and back views.
Building and practicing the second move, the Crossover.
Introducing and practicing the third move, the Tack Annie.
Learning and practicing the fourth move, the Half Break, starting on 8.
Focusing on smaller steps where the heel hits the floor right below the knee for a satisfying sound.
Practicing the stamp-off part of the Tack Annie focusing on rhythm and body movement.
Dancing through the full routine sequence along with the music.

adaptations.difficulty: Hard time hearing where phrases are in the music
adaptations.adjustment: Watch the recommended video on music structure

beliefs.belief: The Shim Sham's relative simplicity allows more people to dance it and use it as a platform for creativity.
You are a dancer before you are a partner dancer.

method.limits: The video is a digital tutorial and does not provide real-time personalized feedback or partner interaction.
